name: Null and Void
description: A documentary assembled from leaked internal footage, whistleblower testimony, and covert recordings inside OmniSol's Tier 1 labor processing facilities, Null and Void presents systematic evidence of cognitive suppression implants installed in workers without informed consent — BCIs configured to reduce pain perception and increase compliance rather than enhance productivity as advertised. The film was assembled by an anonymous collective known only as 'the Residuals' and has never been attributed to a single director. It circulates exclusively on encrypted mesh networks.
cultural_impact: Null and Void is the most-cited film in Shelf activist literature and has become a rallying artifact for the BCI rights movement, with its central image — a worker's compliance graph flatlined at perfect obedience — reproduced on graffiti across M88's lower tiers.
story_hooks: Someone has identified one of the Residuals collective and is selling the information — the party must decide whether to protect the filmmaker or use the lead themselves.
A newly hired OmniSol worker approaches the party after recognizing symptoms from the film in their own behavioral changes post-implant.
A Tier 4 attorney is building a class-action case and needs authenticated copies of the film as evidence — which means someone has to retrieve them from deep in the mesh.
